texts.facts: This writ petition has been filed challenging the order passed by the second respondent dated 01.08.2023, thereby allowed the complaint lodged by the third respondent under Section 23 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizen Act, 2017 (hereinafter referred to as the Act) and cancelled the settlement deed executed by the third respondent in favour of the petitioner's minor daughters. 2. The third respondent got married one Sivagami and she had purchased the propertiess situated at Door No.3/276-12A, 3/276/13 ad measuring 962 sq.ft., and a vacant house plot ad measuring 9481 sq.ft., along with other facilities in Old S.F.No.311A, New S.F.No.102/5 situated at Saravana Nagar, Pidariyur Village, Chennimalai, by the registered sale deed dated 29.08.2001 registered vide document Nos.1088 & 1089 of 2001. Further, they had no issue and subsequently, the said Sivagami died. She had one brother named Marappa Gounder and the said Marappa gounder has one daughter. The petitioner is the son-in-law of the said Marappa Gounder. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3. Due to love and affection, the third respondent agreed to settle the subject property in favour of the petitioner's daughters and also executed the settlement deed dated 19.09.2018 registered vide document No.2703 of 2018. After execution of the settlement deed, the petitioner and his family members driven out the third respondent from the settled property and failed to maintained him. Therefore, the third respondent was suffering from even for his day to day life. 4. Therefore, the third respondent filed a petition under Section 23 of the Act. After conducting fullfledged enquiry, by an order dated 01.08.2023, the second respondent allowed the complaint lodged by the third respondent and cancelled the settlement deed executed in favour of the minor daughters of the petitioner. Thereafter, the third respondent filed a writ petition before this Court in W.P.No.13678 of 2024 for direction to implement the order passed by the second respondent. This Court by an order dated 16.05.2024 directed the Sub Registrar, Erode District to record the order passed by the second respondent dated 01.08.2023. Accordingly, recorded the order passed by the second respondent and the third respondent dealt with the subject property by execution of sale deed in favour of the third party. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that there is no specific clause to maintain the third respondent in the settlement deed. Therefore, the complaint under Section 23 of the Act, itself is not maintainable.
texts.arguments: In support of his contention, he relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sudesh Chhikara Vs. Ramti Devi in Order dated 06.12.2022 in Civil Appeal No. 174 of 2021, which reads as follows:- 12. Sub-section (1) of Section 23 covers all kinds of transfers as is clear from the use of the expression by way of gift or otherwise.
